messages.subject: Model with more than one likelihood
parts:
Hello all

I have a quick question. I read through the inla documentation and had a look at the examples explaining how to formulate a model with more than one likelihood but am still unclear how to code up an inla call for the following case:

We have two random variables, Y1 and Y2. (they have been put into a matrix called 'Data) Both are binomial random variables but they have different Ntrials vectors for each of the random variables. i.e. Y1 could be of length n1 while Y2 is of length n2 (n1 is not equal to n2). So there are two different Ntrials vectors. (below they are 'trials.z' and 'trials.y') How would one specify the inla call?


I tried the following: 

inla(formula, data=Data,
      family=c("binomial", "binomial"),
      Ntrials=list(trials.z, trials.y)   #this MUST BE INCORRECT!
)

and received an error

Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 40, 30


The '40' and '30' relates to the length of the two different Ntrials vectors.

Looking forward to a reply. (I've not added data since the example seems to be fairly simple)

Allan

I have a quick question. I read through the inla documentation and had a look at the examples explaining how to formulate a model with more than one likelihood but am still unclear how to code up an inla call for the following case:

We have two random variables, Y1 and Y2. (they have been put into a matrix called 'Data) Both mbere binomial random variables but they have different Ntrials vectors for each of the random variables. i.e. Y1 could be of length n1 while Y2 is of length n2 (n1 is not equal to n2). So there are two different Ntrials vectors. (below they are 'trials.z' and 'trials.y') How would one specify the inla call?

The outcomes should be stored in a two-column matrix, with (at least) one NA entry for each row, so that the number of rows is the total number of observations; something like

observations <- rbind(cbind(Z, NA), cbind(NA, Y))

Ntrials should then be c(trials.z, trials.y)

You may also need
  control.predictor=list(link=c(rep(1, length(Z)), rep(2, length(Y))))
In your case both likelihoods have the same link function, but in general, this code is needed to tell
INLA which link function to apply for all-NA rows of "observations" for fitted.values output.
 
Finn
